questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Mr. Prakash writes short stories.

options.text: Short stories were written by Mr. Prakash.
Short stories are being written by Mr. Prakash.
Short stories have been written by Mr. Prakash.
Short stories are written by Mr. Prakash.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Mr. Prakash writes short stories."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "short stories" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "writes" to "are written" (present simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Mr. Prakash."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Short stories are written by Mr. Prakash."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Short stories were written by Mr. Prakash." – Incorrect tense (past simple passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"Short stories are being written by Mr. Prakash." – Incorrect tense (present continuous passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"Short stories have been written by Mr. Prakash." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The principal said that he would hold a meeting the next day.

options.text: “Tomorrow, I will hold a meeting,” says the principal.
“A meeting will be held by me,” said the principal.
“I will be holding a meeting tomorrow,” the principal said.
“I will hold a meeting tomorrow,” said the principal.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The principal said that he would hold a meeting the next day.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"that he would hold a meeting" becomes "I will hold a meeting"**
 
 
• Pronoun "he" is changed to "I" to match direct speech.
 
• Verb "would" is changed to "will" to match the future tense in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **"the next day" becomes "tomorrow"**
 
 
• Time expression "the next day" is converted to "tomorrow" for direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "said that"
 
• Converted to: "said", maintaining the reporting structure.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with a period ".".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“I will hold a meeting tomorrow,” said the principal."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Tomorrow, I will hold a meeting," says the principal. 

 
 
• Uses present tense "says" instead of past tense "said".
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "A meeting will be held by me," said the principal. 
 
 
• Changes the active voice to passive voice, which is not a direct speech conversion.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "I will be holding a meeting tomorrow," the principal said. 
 
 
• Uses continuous future tense "will be holding" instead of simple future tense "will hold".

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

(A) They do taste kind of funny.

(B) I’ve done so all my life.

(C) But it keeps them on the knife.

(D) I always eat peas with honey.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (3)** i.e. **DBAC**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the subject "I always eat peas with honey," which is correctly indicated by **part (D).**** **
 
• Following the subject, "I've done so all my life" **(DB)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear what the writer has always done.
 
• **The next part,** "But it keeps them on the knife," starts the explanation about the reason, indicated by (A).
 
• **Ending with **"They do taste kind of funny" (C) completes the sentence by stating the effect of the action.

Therefore, the correct answer is **DBAC.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (ABDC):** This option starts with "They do taste kind of funny But it keeps them on the knife," which makes the sentence incorrect as the explanation starts too early, missing contextual flow.
 
• **Option 2 (BACD):** This option starts with "I've done so all my life They do taste kind of funny," which makes the sentence incorrect as it does not start with the subject.
 
• **Option 4 (CBAD):** This option starts with "But it keeps them on the knife I've done so all my life," which creates a fragmented and confusing sentence structure.

Gita said, “I lost my umbrella.”

options.text: Gita said that she had lost her umbrella.
Gita said that I lost my umbrella.
Gita told me that he lost her umbrella.
Gita expressed that she has lost her umbrella.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** It is used to report what someone said without using their exact words.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• In indirect speech, the past simple tense "lost" changes to past perfect "had lost."
 
• The pronoun "I" is changed to "she" to match the subject "Gita."
 
• The possessive "my" changes to "her" to reflect Gita’s ownership of the umbrella.
 
 
 
• **Correct Indirect Speech:** "Gita said that she had lost her umbrella."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

• **Option 3:** "Gita told me that he lost her umbrella."
 
 
• Incorrect because "he" is wrongly used instead of "she" for Gita.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Gita expressed that she has lost her umbrella."
 
 
• Incorrect because "has lost" should be in past perfect "had lost."
